title: Kinsing_Cryptominer_Incident_Response_Scenario_399
description: Investigate and respond to a Kinsing cryptominer infection on a Linux network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Kinsing malware is a cryptocurrency miner that exploits Linux systems. It spreads through vulnerabilities and installs cryptocurrency miners and rootkits, leading to remote code execution (RCE). The malware targets Apache ActiveMQ and uses various persistence mechanisms. In subsequent training levels, you will need to submit specific values such as service names, process names, and file paths.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You are an incident responder with access to the compromised network. Your entry point is the `miner-host` with the following credentials:
- Hostname: `miner-host`
- Username: `cyrano`
- Password: `cyrano`

Enter the passkey 'start' to begin the scenario.
levels.local_content:
Instructions for local sandbox usage. Your entry point is the `miner-host` with the following credentials:
- Hostname: `miner-host`
- Username: `cyrano`
- Password: `cyrano`

Enter the passkey 'start' to begin the scenario.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the `miner-host` and identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system. Enumerate running services and distinguish legitimate services from malicious miner-related services.
levels.solution: To identify suspicious services, run the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` and look for any services that appear unusual or unauthorized. The Kinsing malware often creates a service named `kinsing-service` or similar.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the status of all services and look for any that appear unusual or unauthorized.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or those that are not part of the standard system services.

levels.title: Analyze Abnormal CPU Utilization
levels.content: Analyze the `miner-host` for abnormal CPU or resource utilization and identify the process responsible. Analyze running processes and correlate resource consumption with potentially malicious activity.
levels.solution: To identify processes consuming excessive resources, run the command `top` or `htop` and look for processes with high CPU usage. The Kinsing malware often creates a process named `kinsing-process` or similar.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use process monitoring tools to identify processes consuming excessive resources.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Run the command `top` or `htop` to monitor CPU usage.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for processes with high CPU usage that do not correspond to known system processes.

levels.title: Locate Malicious Artifacts
levels.content: Locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious activity on the `miner-host`. Correlate suspicious processes or services with files on disk and identify malicious artifacts.
levels.solution: To locate malicious artifacts, investigate the paths and properties of running processes to find associated files. The Kinsing malware often creates files in `/usr/local/sbin/` or `/tmp/` with names like `kinsing` or `kinsing-process`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate the paths and properties of running processes to find associated files.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the directories `/usr/local/sbin/` and `/tmp/` for suspicious files.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for files with unusual names or those that are not part of the standard system files.
